title: Polar and Nonpolar Molecules
short: A molecule is polar when its bond dipoles do not cancel out.
trouble: Students call CO₂ polar because its bonds are polar, missing that its two dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel.

blocks.html: A molecule can contain polar bonds (Polar and Nonpolar Bonds) and still be nonpolar overall. Whether it is depends on its shape, from Molecular Shapes (VSEPR). Molecular polarity matters because it decides how molecules attract each other, which sets boiling points and what dissolves in what.

Treat each bond dipole as an arrow pointing toward the more electronegative atom. Add the arrows. If they cancel, the molecule is nonpolar; if they leave a net arrow, it is polar. Symmetric shapes with identical outer atoms (linear $\mathrm{CO_2}$, trigonal planar $\mathrm{BF_3}$, tetrahedral $\mathrm{CCl_4}$) are nonpolar.

Bond dipoles add like forces in a tug-of-war. In $\mathrm{CO_2}$ the two C=O dipoles are equal and point in exactly opposite directions, so they cancel. In $\mathrm{H_2O}$ the molecule is bent, so the two O–H dipoles both point partly toward oxygen and add up: oxygen's side of the molecule is negative and the hydrogens' side positive. Change one outer atom and the symmetry breaks: $\mathrm{CCl_4}$ is nonpolar, but $\mathrm{CH_3Cl}$ is polar.

blocks.cap: Carbon dioxide: two polar bonds pulling in opposite directions. The net dipole is zero.

blocks.name: ch-vsepr
blocks.cap: Water: the bent shape lets the two bond dipoles add up to a net dipole toward oxygen.

blocks.title: Ammonia
steps: N–H bonds are polar (N 3.04, H 2.20), with $\delta^-$ on N.
The lone pair makes the molecule a pyramid, so all three dipoles tilt toward N.

blocks.title: Carbon tetrachloride
steps: But the four bonds are identical and point to the corners of a tetrahedron.

blocks.html: Calling $\mathrm{CO_2}$ polar because its bonds are polar. Polar bonds are needed for a polar molecule, but not enough: the shape must keep the dipoles from canceling. Check: draw the shape and ask whether you could spin or flip the molecule so that the dipole arrows exactly undo each other.
